target.title: fix(agents): add size limit to LSP message parser
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: The LSP message parser accepted unbounded `Content-Length`
values. A malicious or misbehaving LSP server could send an arbitrarily
large `Content-Length` header, causing unbounded buffer allocation and
memory exhaustion.

**Root cause**: When `Content-Length` exceeded the 10 MB limit, the parser
only skipped the header + separator bytes but kept the declared body in
`session.buffer`. If the oversized body arrived across multiple stream
chunks, the buffer would grow unboundedly.

**Solution**: Add a 10 MB `Content-Length` limit that fully drains the
declared oversized body (header + separator + body bytes) when the frame
is completely buffered, or tracks remaining bytes to skip via
`session.oversizeDrainRemaining` when the body arrives across chunks.

**What changed**: `src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.ts`
- `parseLspMessages`: accepts optional `oversizeDrainRemaining` out-param;
  on oversized frames, drains the full frame or signals remaining bytes
- `handleIncomingData`: drains `session.oversizeDrainRemaining` from raw
  stream data before appending to the parse buffer
- `LspSession` type: added `oversizeDrainRemaining: number`

**What did NOT change**: Valid message parsing, session lifecycle, tool
materialization — all unchanged for frames within the 10 MB limit.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: LSP message parser now fully drains oversized
Content-Length frames instead of only skipping the header, closing the
memory-exhaustion path.

**Real environment tested**: Linux 4.19.112, Node 22.19.0, pnpm 11.2.2

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
npx tsx proof-oversized-lsp-frame.ts
pnpm test src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```text
L2 Proof: Oversized Content-Length Frame Handling

Test 1: Partial oversized frame (header only, no body)
  Content-Length: 10485761 (10.0 MB)
  Buffer size:     28 B
  Remaining bytes: 0 B
  Drain counter:   10.0 MB
  -> Oversized frame detected, buffer discarded OK

Test 2: Full oversized frame + valid message after
  Total input:     10.0 MB
  Messages parsed: 1
  Drain counter:   0 B
  -> Entire oversized frame drained OK
  -> Valid message after oversized frame correctly parsed

Test 3: Multiple sequential oversized frames
  Total input:     20.0 MB
  Messages parsed: 1
  Drain counter:   0 B
  -> Multiple oversized frames drained OK

Summary: All 3 proof scenarios pass. Oversized Content-Length frames
are properly detected and drained; stream alignment is preserved.
```

**Observed result after the fix**: The parser correctly drains oversized
frames. When the full frame is buffered, all body bytes are skipped and
subsequent valid messages are parsed. When only partial data is available,
remaining bytes are tracked and drained from future chunks, keeping
`session.buffer` bounded.

**Before-fix evidence**: Before fix, `parseLspMessages` at line 197 did:
```
remaining = remaining.subarray(headerEnd + headerSeparator.length);
continue;
```
This only skipped the header. Body bytes declared by `Content-Length`
stayed in `session.buffer` and accumulated across stream chunks with no
`\r\n\r\n` separator, leaving the memory-exhaustion path open.

**What was not tested**: A real LSP server sending oversized messages.
The proof calls `parseLspMessages` directly with synthetic data that
exercises the identical code paths a live LSP server would trigger.

**Risk level**: Low — only oversized Content-Length values trigger the new
code path; all existing message sizes use the unchanged happy path.
merge-risk: low

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible — 10 MB is well above realistic LSP message sizes
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations — all 8 existing tests pass unchanged
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation — no docs changes needed
- [x] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary — none
